title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
text: PhysioAnalysis provides comprehensive set spectral analysis tools physiological signal data stored PhysioExperiment objects. vignette covers three core spectral analysis workflows: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) – computing magnitude spectra Power Spectral Density (PSD) – estimating visualizing signal power across frequencies Time-frequency analysis – spectrograms wavelet transforms non-stationary signals

title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
code: library(PhysioCore) library(PhysioAnalysis)

title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
text: begin constructing synthetic PhysioExperiment object known frequency composition can verify spectral analyses.
code: set.seed(42) sr <- 256  # sampling rate in Hz duration <- 4  # seconds n_time <- sr * duration t <- seq(0, duration - 1/sr, by = 1/sr)  # Simulate a 4-channel signal with known frequency components: #   Channel 1: 10 Hz sine (alpha) #   Channel 2: 10 Hz + 25 Hz sine (alpha + beta) #   Channel 3: White noise #   Channel 4: 10 Hz sine + noise signal <- matrix(0, nrow = n_time, ncol = 4) signal[, 1] <- sin(2 * pi * 10 * t) signal[, 2] <- sin(2 * pi * 10 * t) + 0.5 * sin(2 * pi * 25 * t) signal[, 3] <- rnorm(n_time) signal[, 4] <- sin(2 * pi * 10 * t) + 0.3 * rnorm(n_time)  pe <- PhysioExperiment(   assays = list(raw = signal),   colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(     label = c("Ch1_alpha", "Ch2_alpha_beta", "Ch3_noise", "Ch4_alpha_noise")   ),   samplingRate = sr )

title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
text: fftSignals() function computes discrete Fourier transform along time axis default assay stores magnitude spectrum new assay named "fft".
code: pe_fft <- fftSignals(pe)  # The FFT result is stored as a new assay assayNames(pe_fft)  # Access the magnitude spectrum fft_data <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(pe_fft, "fft") dim(fft_data)  # time x channels (frequency bins x channels)

title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
text: magnitude spectrum returned fftSignals() dimensions input data. first half rows corresponds frequencies 0 Hz Nyquist frequency (sampling rate / 2).
code: n <- nrow(fft_data) freqs <- seq(0, sr / 2, length.out = floor(n / 2) + 1)  # Plot magnitude spectrum for channel 1 (should peak at 10 Hz) plot(freqs, fft_data[1:(floor(n/2) + 1), 1],      type = "l", xlab = "Frequency (Hz)", ylab = "Magnitude",      main = "FFT Magnitude - Channel 1 (10 Hz)")

title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
text: plotPSD() function provides convenient way compute visualize power spectral density one channels.
code: # Plot PSD for all channels with log scale plotPSD(pe, channels = 1:4, log_scale = TRUE)  # Plot PSD for a specific frequency range plotPSD(pe, channels = c(1, 2), freq_range = c(1, 50), log_scale = TRUE)  # Linear scale PSD plotPSD(pe, channels = 1:2, log_scale = FALSE, freq_range = c(1, 50))

title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
text: bandPower() function extracts power within predefined custom frequency bands. useful quantifying activity standard EEG bands (delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma).
code: # Extract power in standard EEG bands bp <- bandPower(pe, bands = list(   delta = c(1, 4),   theta = c(4, 8),   alpha = c(8, 13),   beta  = c(13, 30),   gamma = c(30, 100) ))  # The result contains power values for each band and channel bp

title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
text: spectrogram() function computes time-frequency representation signal using Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT). useful analyzing frequency content signal changes time.
code: # Compute spectrogram for channel 1 spec <- spectrogram(pe, window_size = 128, overlap = 0.75, channel = 1)  # The result contains: #   - power: frequency x time power matrix #   - frequencies: frequency vector (Hz) #   - times: time vector (seconds) str(spec)  # Visualize the spectrogram plotSpectrogram(spec, freq_range = c(1, 50))

title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
text: choice window size overlap affects trade-time frequency resolution: Larger windows provide better frequency resolution poorer time resolution. Higher overlap provides smoother temporal estimates cost increased computation. Common window functions include Hanning (default), Hamming, Blackman.
code: # Higher frequency resolution (larger window) spec_high_freq <- spectrogram(pe, window_size = 512, overlap = 0.75, channel = 1) plotSpectrogram(spec_high_freq, freq_range = c(1, 50))  # Higher time resolution (smaller window) spec_high_time <- spectrogram(pe, window_size = 64, overlap = 0.75, channel = 1) plotSpectrogram(spec_high_time, freq_range = c(1, 50))

title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
text: waveletTransform() function uses Morlet wavelets compute time-frequency representation. Compared STFT, wavelet analysis provides better frequency resolution low frequencies better time resolution high frequencies.
code: # Compute wavelet transform for channel 1 wt <- waveletTransform(pe, frequencies = seq(1, 50, by = 0.5), channel = 1)  # The result contains the wavelet power at each frequency and time point str(wt)

title: Spectral Analysis with PhysioAnalysis
text: Hilbert transform computes analytic signal, can used extract instantaneous amplitude (envelope) instantaneous phase.
code: # Compute the analytic signal pe_hilbert <- hilbertTransform(pe)  # Extract instantaneous amplitude (envelope) pe_amp <- instantaneousAmplitude(pe_hilbert)  # Extract instantaneous phase pe_phase <- instantaneousPhase(pe_hilbert)

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: PhysioAnalysis provides suite statistical testing functions designed epoched physiological signal data. vignette covers: Parametric tests – pointwise t-tests ANOVA across epochs Cluster-based permutation tests – non-parametric correction multiple comparisons Effect sizes confidence intervals – Cohen’s d bootstrap CI Multiple comparison correction – FDR, Bonferroni, Holm methods statistical functions operate 4D epoched data (time x channel x epoch x sample) produced epochData().

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
code: library(PhysioCore) library(PhysioAnalysis)

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: create synthetic epoched data known effect demonstrate statistical testing functions.
code: set.seed(123) n_time <- 100      # time points per epoch n_channels <- 4    # number of channels n_epochs <- 40     # total epochs (20 per condition) sr <- 250          # sampling rate  # Create 4D array: time x channel x epoch x sample epochs <- array(rnorm(n_time * n_channels * n_epochs * 1),                 dim = c(n_time, n_channels, n_epochs, 1))  # Add a signal to condition 2 (epochs 21-40) in channels 1-2, # time points 30-60 (simulating an ERP effect) epochs[30:60, 1:2, 21:40, 1] <- epochs[30:60, 1:2, 21:40, 1] + 1.0  pe <- PhysioExperiment(   assays = list(epoched = epochs),   colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(     label = paste0("Ch", 1:n_channels)   ),   samplingRate = sr,   metadata = list(     epoch_tmin = -0.2,     epoch_tmax = 0.2,     epoch_info = S4Vectors::DataFrame(       condition = rep(c("control", "stimulus"), each = 20)     )   ) )

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: tTestEpochs() function performs t-tests time point channel. supports one-sample, two-sample (independent), paired designs.

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: Test whether epoch values differ significantly zero.
code: # One-sample t-test against zero (all epochs) result_one <- tTestEpochs(pe)  # The result contains t-values and p-values as time x channel matrices str(result_one) dim(result_one$t_values)  # 100 x 4 dim(result_one$p_values)  # 100 x 4

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: Compare two conditions (e.g., control vs. stimulus).
code: # Two-sample t-test: control (epochs 1-20) vs stimulus (epochs 21-40) result_two <- tTestEpochs(pe,                           condition1 = 1:20,                           condition2 = 21:40)  # Find time points with significant effects (uncorrected) sig_mask <- result_two$p_values < 0.05 cat("Number of significant time-channel pairs:", sum(sig_mask, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: epochs naturally paired (e.g., pre/post within subjects).
code: result_paired <- tTestEpochs(pe,                              condition1 = 1:20,                              condition2 = 21:40,                              paired = TRUE)

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
code: # Test if stimulus > control result_greater <- tTestEpochs(pe,                               condition1 = 21:40,                               condition2 = 1:20,                               alternative = "greater")

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: anovaEpochs() function performs one-way ANOVA time point channel across multiple conditions.
code: # Create data with 3 conditions set.seed(42) epochs3 <- array(rnorm(n_time * n_channels * 30 * 1),                  dim = c(n_time, n_channels, 30, 1))  # Add effects to condition B and C epochs3[30:60, 1:2, 11:20, 1] <- epochs3[30:60, 1:2, 11:20, 1] + 0.8 epochs3[30:60, 1:2, 21:30, 1] <- epochs3[30:60, 1:2, 21:30, 1] + 1.5  pe3 <- PhysioExperiment(   assays = list(epoched = epochs3),   colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(label = paste0("Ch", 1:n_channels)),   samplingRate = sr,   metadata = list(     epoch_info = S4Vectors::DataFrame(       condition = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 10)     )   ) )  # Run ANOVA using the condition column from epoch_info anova_result <- anovaEpochs(pe3, groups = "condition")  # Results include F-values, p-values, and group means str(anova_result)

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: clusterPermutationTest() function implements non-parametric cluster-based permutation test described Maris Oostenveld (2007). approach corrects multiple comparisons problem maintaining sensitivity effects distributed across time channels.

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: Compute pointwise t-statistics conditions. Threshold t-values identify clusters contiguous significant points. cluster, compute cluster-level statistic (sum t-values). Build null distribution permuting condition labels repeating steps 1-3. Compare observed cluster statistics permutation distribution.
code:
# Run cluster-based permutation test cluster_result <- clusterPermutationTest(   pe,   condition1 = 1:20,   condition2 = 21:40,   n_permutations = 1000,   cluster_threshold = 0.05,   tail = 0,        # two-tailed   seed = 42 )  # Examine results cat("Number of clusters found:", length(cluster_result$clusters), "
") cat("Cluster p-values:", cluster_result$cluster_p, "
")  # The cluster_mask indicates which time-channel points belong to # significant clusters (p < 0.05) sig_points <- sum(cluster_result$cluster_mask) cat("Significant time-channel points:", sig_points, "

text: one condition provided, test uses sign-flipping permutations test zero.
code: cluster_one <- clusterPermutationTest(   pe,   condition1 = 21:40,  # stimulus epochs only   n_permutations = 500,   seed = 42 )

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
code: # The permutation distribution is available for inspection hist(cluster_result$permutation_distribution,      breaks = 30,      main = "Permutation Distribution of Max Cluster Statistic",      xlab = "Max cluster statistic")  # Add observed cluster statistics abline(v = abs(cluster_result$cluster_stats), col = "red", lwd = 2)

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: effectSize() function computes Cohen’s d time point channel, 95% confidence intervals.
code: # One-sample effect size (d = mean / sd) es_one <- effectSize(pe, condition1 = 21:40)  # Two-sample effect size (pooled SD) es_two <- effectSize(pe, condition1 = 1:20, condition2 = 21:40)  # Glass's delta (using control group SD) es_glass <- effectSize(pe, condition1 = 21:40, condition2 = 1:20,                        pooled = FALSE)  # Examine effect sizes with confidence intervals str(es_two) # d:        Cohen's d matrix (time x channel) # ci_lower: Lower 95% CI # ci_upper: Upper 95% CI

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: bootstrapCI() function computes bootstrap confidence intervals mean across epochs. particularly useful ERP analysis.
code: # Bootstrap CI with 1000 iterations boot_result <- bootstrapCI(pe,                            n_bootstrap = 1000,                            ci_level = 0.95,                            condition = 21:40,  # stimulus epochs                            seed = 42)  # The result contains the mean and CI bounds str(boot_result)  # Plot the ERP with bootstrap CI for channel 1 plot(boot_result$times, boot_result$mean[, 1],      type = "l", lwd = 2,      xlab = "Time (s)", ylab = "Amplitude",      main = "ERP with 95% Bootstrap CI") polygon(c(boot_result$times, rev(boot_result$times)),         c(boot_result$ci_lower[, 1], rev(boot_result$ci_upper[, 1])),         col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.2), border = NA)

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: correctPValues() function applies standard correction methods p-value matrices vectors.
code:
# Get uncorrected p-values from t-test p_uncorrected <- result_two$p_values  # False Discovery Rate (Benjamini-Hochberg) p_fdr <- correctPValues(p_uncorrected, method = "fdr")  # Bonferroni correction p_bonf <- correctPValues(p_uncorrected, method = "bonferroni")  # Holm's step-down procedure p_holm <- correctPValues(p_uncorrected, method = "holm")  # Compare number of significant results cat("Uncorrected:", sum(p_uncorrected < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "
") cat("FDR:", sum(p_fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "
") cat("Bonferroni:", sum(p_bonf < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "
") cat("Holm:", sum(p_holm < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "
")

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: findSignificantWindows() function identifies contiguous time periods significant effects, useful summarizing results.
code: # Get the time vector times <- seq(-0.2, 0.2, length.out = n_time)  # Find significant windows for channel 1 (FDR-corrected) windows <- findSignificantWindows(   p_values = p_fdr[, 1],   times = times,   alpha = 0.05,   min_duration = 0.02  # at least 20 ms )  # Display the significant windows print(windows) # Columns: start, end, duration, min_p

title: Statistical Testing with PhysioAnalysis
text: typical statistical analysis workflow ERP data:
code: # 1. Start with epoched data #    (assuming pe is already epoched with condition labels)  # 2. Compute pointwise t-test t_result <- tTestEpochs(pe, condition1 = 1:20, condition2 = 21:40)  # 3. Apply cluster-based permutation test for correction cluster_result <- clusterPermutationTest(   pe,   condition1 = 1:20,   condition2 = 21:40,   n_permutations = 1000,   seed = 42 )  # 4. Compute effect sizes es <- effectSize(pe, condition1 = 1:20, condition2 = 21:40)  # 5. Compute bootstrap CI for each condition boot_ctrl <- bootstrapCI(pe, condition = 1:20, seed = 42) boot_stim <- bootstrapCI(pe, condition = 21:40, seed = 42)  # 6. Report significant clusters for (i in seq_along(cluster_result$clusters)) {   cat(sprintf("Cluster %d: stat = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",               i, cluster_result$cluster_stats[i],               cluster_result$cluster_p[i])) }
